correctness.rationale: The PSD trace bound characterizes the low-mixing concentration regime with ties. In high mixing the rank-one determinant lemma gives a unique secular root, a strictly concave fixed-root budget problem with globally sufficient KKT equations, and a unique cutoff determining optimum, including the zero-self-retention boundary. The entry thresholds and 4-patch eigenvalue were checked symbolically and by a standalone program; the analytical argument covers all n and all permitted real parameters.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text inspection of the nearest prior reserve growth and allocation papers and source/alias/weighted-cost searches found no result equivalent to the complete heterogeneous weighted-budget resource-entry staircase. Delmas et al. (2023) analyze the same disassortative rank-one mixing template but with unweighted capped group-mass constraints, and their optimizers and feasible domains differ. Generic rank-one secular formulas and spectral concavity are known and excluded from novelty. Historical priority is provisional.
residual_risks: Priority is provisional: general matrix-allocation, ecological investment or economic resource optimization results outside accessible corpus could imply this formula.
The closest disassortative vaccination theory uses the same rank-one matrix type, though a different feasible set; future broader treatment might include arbitrary linear costs.
The model is an idealized growth proxy and says nothing directly about stochastic reserve persistence.

value.rationale: The exact heterogeneity-dependent entry thresholds answer a motivated ecological resource-design question, classify optimum allocations for arbitrary patch count with sharp saturation and tie boundaries, and give an exact four-patch instance in which the least efficient patch is never worth funding. Generality and threshold sensitivity go beyond numerical parameter fitting or a trivial substitution. Only linearized growth is optimized; ecological persistence is not asserted.
